text:
maria: Heads up — during the EU canary shift this morning we saw repeated canary flip-flop after nodes in eu-west-2 were drained one AZ at a time. It looks like GPU pods got evicted and then rescheduled into the remaining AZ, which then pushed capacity over a threshold and the canary rollback triggered.
aj: ugh. do we have the drain sequence? was this gitops-triggered or manual maintenance?
maria: gitops-triggered by the terraform change that applied a new nodepool taint/label strategy. The reconciler rolled out the nodepool update and the autoscaler started evicting pods AZ-by-AZ. infra-bot posted: `kubelet: eviction: "pods" reason: "NodePressure"` in multiple nodes.
loren: log snippets looked like this:
```
I0301 08:12:33.123 kubelet_node_status.go:200] Node eu-w2-azb drained: evicting 6 pods (3 gpus)
I0301 08:12:55.456 eviction_controller.go:88] Evicted pod model-serving-abc-12 for reason: NodeDrain
```
sam: so the canary health check sensitivity + rollout policy caused immediate rollback when p95 latency spiked. Canary was 10% and probe failures >5 caused rollback.
neel: two problems colliding: (1) terraform change changed node taints so pods couldn't be packed across AZs, (2) gitops reconciler applied sequentially per-az which created a transient single-AZ pressure.
aj: concrete mitigation suggestions?
loren: short-term: pause the gitops rollouts for the nodepool PR and/or mark the PR as `manual-apply` so we can apply az-by-az with capacity planning. Also patch the canary rollout config to add a longer stabilization window (increase `analysisInterval` / `maxUnhealthy` thresholds).
maria: agreed. long-term: we should add a preflight check in the infra CI that simulates drain impact (estimate GPU pod packing) before GitOps flips the new nodepool. Also add a gate that prevents reconciler from draining >1 AZ at once for GPU-backed services.
sam: we can also change the progressive delivery strategy for GPU-backed workloads to prefer blue/green or staggered cutovers instead of a small canary percentage. Canary is brittle when single-AZ pressure changes.
aj: action items: (1) disable auto-apply for the nodepool PR (maria), (2) open a gitops preflight check PR (aj), (3) temporary canary policy relax (loren), (4) run a capacity simulation for eu-west-2 (neel).
maria: I'll disable auto-apply now. @aj can you add the preflight runner? maybe a k8s admission-like job that estimates GPU bin-packing from current pods/requests.
aj: yep, I’ll prototype a `drain-impact` job in infra-ci. Plan: run it on PRs that touch nodepool/taints/labels, output a simple risk score (low/medium/high) and block auto-apply for medium+; PR will post comment with packing summary.
neel: packing estimator idea: iterate pods with GPU requests, try a first-fit bin pack across AZ-capacity from cloud provider APIs, report headroom. I'll write a small lambda.
loren: for rollout config changes I pushed a small patch to the canary analysis to add a `stabilizationWindow` of 10m and reduce failure sensitivity: `failureThreshold` -> 10% of traffic for 2 consecutive intervals. That should stop immediate rollback on transient evictions.
sam: also add a fallback policy: if model-serving fails due to evictions, route traffic to a pre-warmed fallback cluster (dedicated capacity) for that org. Not always possible but worth wiring.
infra-bot: deploybot: stopped automatic rollout for nodepool/az-labels PR #542 by request of maria.
maria: we'll schedule a controlled maintenance window tonight to apply nodepool changes in eu-west-2 with on-call and capacity planner in loop. During the maintenance we'll: (a) cordon one AZ at a time, (b) increase replica counts on remaining AZs temporarily, (c) switch GPU scheduling to `binpack` smoothing via node affinity adjustments, (d) keep canary at 0% until stable, then do blue/green.
aj: timeline: start 23:00 UTC, duration 90m. I'll create the ops-runbook and checklist.
neel: I'll deliver the packing estimator by EOD and run a preflight against the current PR branch.
loren: after we stabilize, we should add two GitOps policy changes: - reconciliation throttle: `maxConcurrentReconciles: 1` per-nodepool that touches taints/labels - plan check: require `drain-impact` job passing for auto-apply true.
amaria: agreed. Also let's add a Helm hook to model-serving chart that delays readiness probe for 30s during node drain to reduce flapping (only for GPU nodes). Something like: `preStop: sleep 30` and `readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds: 30` for gpu workloads.
sam: note: readability vs fast fail — keep probes long enough to avoid false positives but short enough for real outages. We'll baseline with perf tests.
aj: I'll open the preflight PR + runbook now. tagging owners in PR.
maria: thanks all. follow-ups: aj PR #/link, neel packing report, loren monitor changes to canary policy. We'll reconvene in #eng-infra after the maintenance window. :white_check_mark:
